claim: Church-style PPLs make a generative model plus conditioning the unit of thought: evaluation is sampling, query is conditional sampling, mem gives memoised random functions. The founding paper has no human data and only small inference examples.
agent_test: Compare a scaffold step that writes a small generative model then conditions, against plain CoT on uncertain-evidence tasks at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Probabilistic-program concept learning (BPL) matches humans on one-shot character classification: 3.3% error vs 4.5% humans (N=40) vs 13.5% deep convnet; fewer than 25% of judges beat chance in visual Turing tests. Numbers rest on one paper (paywalled, not re-opened) plus a recalled line.
agent_test: Analogue: few-shot rule induction (ARC-like) with program-structured hypotheses vs direct answer.

claim: RSA (Frank & Goodman 2012) predicts speaker and listener bets closely (r=0.98 and 0.99; 0.87 after removing 0 and 100 bets). Boundary: deeper recursion in only about 15% of participants; chance-level in some paradigms.
agent_test: Test a what-would-a-speaker-mean step on ambiguity benchmarks at equal tokens.
audit_note: Numbers r=0.98 (speaker), 0.99 (listener), 0.87 after removing 0/100 verified in Frank & Goodman 2012; 15% deeper recursion and chance-level in some paradigms verified in Goodman & Frank 2016 review (which cites others' studies); minor: the two main papers share authors and the first is the founding study; Waldon & Degen 2021 does not address the boundary.

claim: Translating language to a probabilistic program with an LLM, then running inference, tracks human graded judgments better than LLM-only: NIPE r=0.927 vs GPT-4 0.658 vs GPT-3.5 0.100 (n=46, re-verified); BToM belief statements r=0.92 vs 0.19 for non-mentalizer (N=100, re-verified).
agent_test: On social-reasoning items, compare LLM-translated model plus sampler vs the same LLM with CoT at matched tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The 2023 rational-meaning-construction proposal (Wong et al.) is illustrative only: no benchmark table, no head-to-head with plain LLMs.
agent_test: Do not cite as evidence of gain; use as a design pattern only.

claim: The 2025 model-synthesis architecture (Wong et al.) fits human judgments within the human split-half 95% CI in three sports-vignette experiments, with LM-only baselines worse, most in the open-world experiment. Exact R2 values not extracted.
agent_test: Agent builds a vignette-specific model on demand vs direct judgment; score against human data.

claim: Sampling many LLM-written programs and choosing by expected information gain beats single samples in Battleship: k=1 EIG 0.65-0.66 (grammar 0.36; human mean 1.27, re-verified), near human mean at k=5, above it at k=10 (not re-verified). Textual board beat visual board. Many sampled programs are low fidelity (40% CodeLlama, 33% GPT-4). Tested to k=50 with CodeLlama-7b and gpt-4-0613 only: EIG passes the human mean at k=10 and falls short of the best human questions; GPT-4V adds nothing over no-board. No frontier model and no cost curve.
schema_part: O (generate many, score by value of information)
agent_test: Question-asking tasks: k sampled questions scored by EIG vs one question at equal tokens.

claim: Sequential Monte Carlo with an expensive check raises constraint satisfaction over the base LM (10 particles, re-verified): goal inference 0.063 to 0.419, molecules 0.132 to 0.577, text-to-SQL 0.531 to 0.620. Gain is task-dependent: text-to-SQL Full IS 0.618 vs Full SMC 0.620, so resampling adds nothing there. Data-science gain is small at 5 particles (0.224 vs 0.204) and clear from 10 (0.285 vs 0.223, 8B model); the 70B figure 0.346 vs 0.407 stays ambiguous, and two appendix tables disagree (0.225 vs 0.285).
agent_test: Particle-style branch-and-prune with a programmatic checker vs best-of-N at equal tokens.
audit_note: All figures check out against Loula et al. 2025 (Tables 2, 4, 5), but every listed source for them is that one paper (or Lew et al. 2023 from the same Mansinghka lab, which has none of these numbers), so the claim rests on a single study.

claim: SMC Control and the earlier SMC Steering are not statistically distinguishable on text-to-SQL (0.620 vs 0.607, overlapping intervals; 10 vs 5 particles).
agent_test: Treat as no evidence of improvement over a simple rerank.

claim: Resampling helps on some tasks only (10 particles): on goal inference grammar-only SMC is 0.401 vs grammar-only IS 0.083, but on molecules grammar-only SMC (0.205) is below Full IS (0.404). The expensive potential is the main driver.
agent_test: Ablate checker only vs checker plus resampling on our tasks.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM-written Stan programs: BoxLM (GPT-4) matches expert ELPD on Eight schools (-30.42 vs -30.70), Dugongs (23.40 vs 22.52), Surgical (-38.03 vs -40.29) but is far worse on Peregrine (-173.11 vs expert -142.19 in BoxLM; -112.60 in the RefineStat paper). The two papers use different expert baselines. Peregrine expert baselines differ across papers because they are different datasets (BoxLM: real 40-year counts, -142.19; RefineStat: simulated 9 years, -112.60). On the RefineStat set, o3 matches the expert on 3 of 5 datasets.
agent_test: Do not trust cross-paper ELPD tables; re-run on one fixed expert set.

claim: RefineStat raises the share of generated programs that run from 0.10 to 0.45-0.50 (re-verified), but with DQ-7B its ELPD is far below expert on Dugongs (8.35 vs 22.43) and Surgical (-114.29 vs -39.73). Matching experts holds only on Eight schools and GP.
agent_test: Report executable rate and final score separately.

claim: Ellis (2023): LLM-proposed hypotheses plus Bayesian reweighting fit human concept learning: logical concepts R2=0.81 at 100 proposals (112 concepts, 1596 participants), Number Game R2 about 0.95 vs 8 humans, with 50-100 proposals vs over 5000 hypotheses classically. Raw GPT-4 differs from humans.
agent_test: Few-shot rule tasks: LLM proposes 100 rules, evidence reweights, vs direct answer at equal tokens.

claim: Online rule revision with LLM-proposed fuzzy rules fits humans better than hard rules or batch inference (R2 0.57 vs 0.10 vs 0.05) and beats a direct ReAct LLM (6.55/8 vs 4.60/8; humans 5.26/8).
agent_test: Interactive discovery tasks: iterative rule revision vs plain agent loop.

claim: Humans beat GPT-3 on structured thought generation in every condition (blind raters N=393, p<0.001), and the LLM-as-planner solved none of the most constrained problems. Model is old.
agent_test: Context only.

claim: CLIPS pragmatic instruction following with inverse planning is 1.26-1.68x faster and 1.18-1.58x cheaper than baselines, but human-rating correlations vary widely (r=0.15 to 0.96).
agent_test: Weak; skip unless pragmatic instruction following becomes a target.

claim: Criticisms of Bayesian cognitive models were opened: Marcus and Davis (2013) show the Frank and Goodman fit changes sharply under other decision rules and that the poetry and movie priors were post hoc; Bowers and Davis (2012) argue flexibility; Griffiths et al. (2012) answer that priors are measurable and models testable. No systematic quantitative re-fit across studies was found.
agent_test: Fix model and priors before checking fit when the agent builds probabilistic models.

claim: Counterfactual simulation with noise explains causal judgments better than a deterministic model: r=.96 RMSE 13.46 (noise 0.9) vs r=.86 RMSE 28.15 (noise 0), about N=41 per judgment type.
agent_test: Causal items: simulate-with-noise counterfactuals vs plain explanation.

claim: LLM-elicited priors gave near-identical posteriors to manual weak priors, on one model class only.
agent_test: Out of scope.

claim: On Bayesian-network questions, GPT-4 CoT accuracy falls from 78 percent (2 variables) to 7 percent (10 variables), while LLM-written ProbLog code stays 96 to 100 percent and Monte Carlo code 88 to 100 percent (900 test instances). On the small CLADDER adaptation (100 items) GPT-4 CoT few-shot is already 96 percent vs PAL 98.
schema_part: S (solver call when many interacting variables)
agent_test: Gate: if more than about 5 interacting quantities, write code and run it instead of reasoning in text.

claim: No study found compares an LLM-built probabilistic model plus sampling against long CoT from a frontier or reasoning model at equal tokens. Wong 2023 and 2025 and Large Language Bayes report no token counts; the best 2025 baseline is Llama-3.1-70B CoT.
schema_part: G (do not claim a gain without a matched baseline)
agent_test: Run the agent with and without the probabilistic route at the same token budget before adopting it.

claim: A frontier reasoning model (o3) writes Stan programs close to expert level on textbook PosteriorDB problems: ELPD within noise of expert on Eight schools, Dugongs and Surgical, worse on Peregrine (-133.29 vs -112.60) and GP (-34.95 vs -26.53).
agent_test: Scaffold gain for programme writing is likely largest for small models.

claim: Hypothesis proposal plus verification on ARC with GPT-4: 17 percent direct, 23 program only, 30 with LLM-summarised hypotheses, 33 human-selected, 45 human-written hypotheses (100 training tasks). Ellis-style Bayesian reweighting has not been tested on ARC.
agent_test: Propose several rules, check each against the examples, keep what passes all.

claim: No many-labs or cross-language replication of Frank and Goodman 2012 or Lake 2015 was found or opened. A close replication (Qing and Franke 2015) is only seen in a search snippet.
agent_test: Treat RSA fit numbers as one-lab results.

claim: Wong 2025 reports model-human R2 for LM-only baselines only in figures, so the LM-only baseline numbers cannot be quoted; MSA self-consistency across Exp1 and Exp2 is about R2 0.95 to 0.98.
agent_test: Do not cite exact LM-only R2.

claim: Cost anchors: generating 1024 Stan models with Llama-3.3-70B took 10 to 15 minutes on one A100; SMC data-science runs needed 4 H100 GPUs; BLInD authors say solver time is milliseconds against seconds of LLM generation. None was compared with CoT cost.
agent_test: Budget the model-writing step, not the solver.
